EXPLANATION: The strong pair at 1613 and 1567 cm⁻¹ fits conjugated C=C stretching in a 1,3-butadiene framework (FRQ-001), while the low-frequency bands at 658 and 586 cm⁻¹ lie in the typical C–Cl stretching region for heavily chlorinated molecules (cf. GFQ-046, GFQ-041; source: nakamoto2008infrared). The 855 cm⁻¹ band can also be attributed to C–Cl related modes in polychloro alkenes. Absence of nitrile (~2300 cm⁻¹) or carbonyl (~1700–1850 cm⁻¹) features disfavors candidates bearing CN or C=O groups (GFQ-008), and lack of clear C–F signature argues against F-containing options. Hexachloro-1,3-butadiene (candidate 7) best matches this pattern among the list.
